rows.assignRule: The corner clearing that holds Gustave's keep. The Marquise sets up first, so the role is fixed as soon as the keep is placed, before any other faction sets up. When Gustave is not seated, the corner is chosen by rule at map load: the corner with the lowest Root clearing number.
rows._notes: Assignment order for every role: Lumière, the Monolith, the Axons (Visages, Sirène, The Reacher), Old Lumière, Esquie's Nest and the Flying Manor, Stone Wave Cliffs, then the Sacred River tag. Roles are fixed for the whole game. 'Path distance' everywhere counts steps along paths; rivers are not paths. The roster's 'a chosen corner' is read as chosen by rule (lowest Root clearing number) so bot-only games and tests repeat; a setup-screen pick could replace it later.

rows.assignRule: The corner Root itself treats as diagonally opposite Lumière (the one normal Marquise setup leaves without a warrior, and the one Bird dominance pairs with it). On a map where Root has no such pairing, the corner farthest from Lumière by path distance; ties go to the lowest Root clearing number. The Paintress's first roost is forced here.

One of the two corners left after Lumière and the Monolith. The Nest is the one that has a Stone Wave Cliffs candidate (a clearing 1-2 steps away by path that is not a corner, not a Monolith path neighbour and not Old Lumière); if both or neither have one, the one with the lower Root clearing number. The other corner is the Flying Manor.
rows._notes: The roster says only that the Nest and the Flying Manor are the other two corners; splitting by 'has a Cliffs candidate, then lower clearing number' is the simplest rule that always leaves Stone Wave Cliffs a valid clearing.

rows.assignRule: The last corner, once Lumière, the Monolith and Esquie's Nest are assigned. Clea's home corner is forced here.

A clearing 1-2 steps by path from Esquie's Nest that is not a corner, not a path neighbour of the Monolith and not Old Lumière. Nearest first (1 step before 2), then the lowest Root clearing number. If none qualifies, the nearest clearing to the Nest that is not a corner, not a Monolith neighbour and not Old Lumière.
rows._notes: Excluding corners and Old Lumière (and the tie-breaks) is this sheet's choice, so Florrie never shares a clearing with another rock or a faction home.

rows.assignRule: The most central ruin clearing: among ruin clearings that are not corners and not Monolith path neighbours, the one with the smallest total path distance to every other clearing; ties go to the lowest Root clearing number. If no ruin qualifies, the most central clearing by the same measure that is not a corner or a Monolith neighbour.
rows._notes: 'Central' is measured as the smallest total path distance, and Monolith neighbours are excluded so Old Lumière never takes an Axon's name. In the no-ruin fallback there is no ruin to Explore, so Dorrie is claimed by entering, as with an emptied ruin.

rows.assignRule: The Axons are the Monolith's path neighbours at map load, taken in order of Root clearing number: the first is Visages, the second Sirène, the third The Reacher. Rivers are not paths, and closed Mountain paths do not count. A fourth or later neighbour gets no Axon name but is still a Monolith neighbour for every rule that reads adjacency.
rows._notes: The White-Haired Man's Ring and Gustave's Beachhead read Monolith adjacency directly; the Axon names label the same clearings on the Ring overlay. The optional v1.1 Monolith Barrier reads Visages and Sirène.

rows.assignRule: The second Monolith path neighbour by Root clearing number (see Visages). Lune's Parents' Journal goes in the forest beside it. There is none on a map where the Monolith has only one open path neighbour; the Journal is then tagged where it lies.
The third Monolith path neighbour by Root clearing number, when there is one (see Visages).

Every clearing a river touches; on Lake, every clearing on the lake shore. It is a tag drawn as a river of chroma, not a place name: these clearings keep their own names and may also hold another role.
rows.count: all river clearings (0 on a map with no river)
rows._notes: No v1 rule reads this tag. Monoco's Sacred River Rebirth is named after it, and Esquie's v1.1 Florrie power (rivers count as paths for him) runs along it.
